title: A rational function with a hole and two asymptotes

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Find every real zero of ff. Give a reason why x=−2x = -2 is not a zero of ff.

rubric.point: The zero <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, and the reason that <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -2</annotation></semantics></math> is not in the domain of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -2</annotation></semantics></math> makes the denominator <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math> only; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(-2)</annotation></semantics></math> is undefined (a hole), so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math> is not a zero

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2(x + 2)(x - 1)}{(x + 1)(x + 2)}</annotation></semantics></math>. The numerator is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -2</annotation></semantics></math>, but <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -2</annotation></semantics></math> also makes the denominator <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>, so it is not in the domain. The only real zero is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Find limx→−2f(x)\lim_{x \to -2} f(x). Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.point: The common factor canceled and the limit <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math> stated in limit notation
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2(x - 1)}{x + 1}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne -2</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -2} f(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2(-3)}{-1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 6</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: For <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne -2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2(x - 1)}{x + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -2} f(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{2(-2 - 1)}{-2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{-6}{-1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 6</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Write the behavior of ff on each side of x=−1x = -1 using limit notation.

rubric.point: Both one-sided limits correct, in full limit notation
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -1^-} f(x) = \infty</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -1^+} f(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\infty</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: Near <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1</annotation></semantics></math>, the numerator <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2(x - 1)</annotation></semantics></math> is close to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-4</annotation></semantics></math>. Left of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 1 < 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is a large positive number: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -1^-} f(x) = \infty</annotation></semantics></math>. Right of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 1 > 0</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -1^+} f(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Write the end behavior of ff using limit notation, and give a reason for it.

rubric.point: Both end-behavior limits equal <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, with a reason from the leading terms
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to \infty} f(x) = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -\infty} f(x) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, because the degrees are equal and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2x^2}{x^2} = 2</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: The numerator and denominator both have degree <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, and the quotient of their leading terms is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2x^2}{x^2} = 2</annotation></semantics></math>. So <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to \infty} f(x) = 2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>→</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x \to -\infty} f(x) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: Solve f(x)=g(x)f(x) = g(x). Give every solution correct to three decimal places.

rubric.point: All three solutions, to three decimal places, and no extra solution at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1</annotation></semantics></math> or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -2</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: Graph <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = f(x)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = g(x)</annotation></semantics></math> in a window wide enough to show every crossing (for example <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-6 \le x \le 6</annotation></semantics></math>) and find the intersections: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3.125</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx -3.125</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.363</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 0.363</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.762</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \approx 1.762</annotation></semantics></math>. Neither <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> nor <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math> is a solution, since <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is undefined there.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: Is the rate of change of ff increasing or decreasing on the interval [2,5][2, 5]? Give a reason using the average rates of change of ff on [2,3.5][2, 3.5] and [3.5,5][3.5, 5].

rubric.point: Decreasing, with both average rates of change found and compared
accept: the average rates are about <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.296</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.296</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[2, 3.5]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.148</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.148</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>3.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[3.5, 5]</annotation></semantics></math>; they decrease, so the rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(2) = \frac{2}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>10</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(3.5) = \frac{10}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(5) = \frac{4}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. The average rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[2, 3.5]</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>1.5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(3.5) - f(2)}{1.5}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>0.296</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 0.296</annotation></semantics></math>, and on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>3.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[3.5, 5]</annotation></semantics></math> it is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3.5</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>1.5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(5) - f(3.5)}{1.5}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>0.148</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 0.148</annotation></semantics></math>. Over these equal-length intervals the average rates decrease, so the rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[2, 5]</annotation></semantics></math> (the graph is concave down there).
